label: Artifact
summary: The artifact whose kill list the window shows.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data source of the kill list window, and its name appears in the window title text '<artifact name> Kills'.

label: Kills
summary: The list of kills the kill list window shows.
details: Going by its name and its single use as the data source of the kill list window in gui/window_kill_list.gui. The game documents nothing more.

label: This kill list window
summary: The kill list window itself, as an object that can be handed on.
details: Going by its name and by how other types' Self functions are used (passed as an argument to other functions). Vanilla never uses it on this window; the game documents nothing more.

label: This artifact entry
summary: The artifact entry of the court scene editor that is being edited, handed to a function.
details: Vanilla passes it to the editor functions that store an edited artifact description, slot type or locator when the player finishes typing. How it differs from Self is not documented.

label: This artifact entry
summary: The artifact entry of the court scene editor, handed to a function.
details: Vanilla passes it to the functions that fold or unfold the entry and ask whether it is unfolded, and uses that to pick which frame (image state) of an element is shown and to show or hide a part of the editor.

label: This artifact type
summary: The artifact type itself, as an object that can be handed on.
details: Going by its name and by how other AccessSelf functions are used. Vanilla never uses it on this type; the game documents nothing more.

label: Artifact type key
summary: The key (internal name) of the artifact type, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as button text and as tooltip in the artifact helper window, a tool window for picking an artifact's type.

label: This artifact type
summary: The artifact type, handed to a function.
details: Vanilla passes it to the artifact helper window's functions that select a type and that check whether a type is the selected one (used for a button's pressed state).

label: This artifact visual type
summary: The artifact visual type itself, as an object that can be handed on.
details: Going by its name and by how other AccessSelf functions are used. Vanilla never uses it on this type; the game documents nothing more.

label: Visual type key
summary: The key (internal name) of the artifact visual type, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as button text and as tooltip in the artifact helper window.

label: This artifact visual type
summary: The artifact visual type, handed to a function.
details: Vanilla passes it to the artifact helper window's functions that select a visual type and that check whether it is the selected one (used for a button's pressed state).

label: This asset entry
summary: The asset entry of the court scene editor that is being edited, handed to a function.
details: Vanilla passes it to the editor functions that store an edited asset description, name or locator when the player finishes typing. How it differs from Self is not documented.

label: This asset entry
summary: The asset entry of the court scene editor, handed to a function.
details: Vanilla passes it to the functions that fold or unfold the entry and that read its description, which is shown as a text (or the word Asset when the description is empty).

label: This vassal list
summary: The assigned vassal list itself, as an object that can be handed on.
details: Going by its name and by how other AccessSelf functions are used. Vanilla never uses it on this type; the game documents nothing more.

label: Clear selection
summary: Empties the list of selected vassals.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it when a button is clicked in the tax slot vassals window. Going by its name, the vassals stay assigned; only the selection is dropped.

label: Levy breakdown
summary: The breakdown of one vassal's levy contribution, as data for a tooltip or list.
details: Going by its name and its single use: vanilla sets it as the data source of an element, giving it a vassal from the list. The game documents nothing more about what the breakdown holds.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The vassal (a list entry of the window) to break down.

label: Levy contribution
summary: A number giving how much levy the given vassal contributes.
details: Vanilla shows it in a localization text of the tax slot vassal window, for each vassal in the list. The exact unit is not documented.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The vassal (a list entry of the window) to look at.

label: Levy share
summary: A number giving the given vassal's levy share, used to fill a progress bar.
details: Vanilla wraps it in a conversion to a progress bar value, so the bar shows the vassal's share. Going by its name, the number is a percentage.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The vassal (a list entry of the window) to look at.

label: Selected vassals
summary: The list of vassals currently selected in the tax slot vassals window.
details: Vanilla counts it in a text ('N vassals are removed as taxpayers'), enables a button only when it has entries, and shows a hint when it is empty.

label: Tax breakdown
summary: The breakdown of one vassal's tax contribution, as data for a tooltip or list.
details: Going by its name and its single use: vanilla sets it as the data source of an element, giving it a vassal from the list. The game documents nothing more about what the breakdown holds.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The vassal (a list entry of the window) to break down.

label: Tax contribution
summary: A number giving how much tax the given vassal contributes.
details: Vanilla shows it with two decimals in a localization text of the tax slot vassal window, for each vassal in the list. The exact unit is not documented.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The vassal (a list entry of the window) to look at.

label: Tax share
summary: A number giving the given vassal's tax share, used to fill a progress bar.
details: Vanilla wraps it in a conversion to a progress bar value, so the bar shows the vassal's share. Going by its name, the number is a percentage.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The vassal (a list entry of the window) to look at.

label: Is vassal selected
summary: Whether the given vassal is currently selected in the list.
details: Vanilla uses it to show or hide parts of a vassal's row in the tax slot vassals window.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The vassal (a list entry of the window) to check.

label: Select all vassals
summary: Selects every vassal in the list.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it when a button is clicked in the tax slot vassals window. Going by its name, it fills the selection that GetSelectedCharacters returns.

label: This vassal list
summary: The assigned vassal list itself, as an object that can be handed on.
details: Going by its name and by how other types' Self functions are used (passed as an argument to other functions). Vanilla never uses it on this type; the game documents nothing more.

label: Local units
summary: The list of units the attach-to-army window offers.
details: Vanilla uses it as the list that fills the window in gui/window_army.gui. Going by its name, these are the units at the army's location.

label: This attach window
summary: The attach-to-army window itself, as an object that can be handed on.
details: Going by its name and by how other AccessSelf functions are used. Vanilla never uses it on this window; the game documents nothing more.

label: Attach to selected
summary: Attaches to the selected unit.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it when a button is clicked in the attach-to-army window. Which army is attached to which is not documented here.

label: Selected army
summary: The army currently selected in the attach-to-army window.
details: Vanilla builds the window's title from it: 'Attach to <army name>'.

label: Has selected unit
summary: Whether a unit is selected in the attach-to-army window.
details: Vanilla uses it to show an element and to enable a button only when something is selected.

label: Close window
summary: Hides the attach-to-army window.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it when buttons of the army window are clicked. Going by its name, it closes the attach window; the game documents nothing more.

label: Is selected unit
summary: Whether the given unit is the selected one.
details: Vanilla uses it for the pressed state of a unit's button in the attach-to-army window.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The unit (a list entry of the window) to check.

label: Select unit
summary: Makes the given unit the selected one.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it when a unit's button is clicked in the attach-to-army window.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The unit (a list entry of the window) to select.

label: This attach window
summary: The attach-to-army window itself, as an object that can be handed on.
details: Going by its name and by how other types' Self functions are used (passed as an argument to other functions). Vanilla never uses it on this window; the game documents nothing more.

label: This attribute
summary: The attribute object itself, as an object that can be handed on.
details: Attribute belongs to the game's internal GUI engine group. Going by the name and by how other AccessSelf functions are used; vanilla never uses it on this type.

label: Attribute name
summary: The name of a portrait attribute, as text.
details: Attribute belongs to the portrait editor, a development tool of the game's engine. Vanilla shows this name as the label and the tooltip of each slider in the editor's list of attribute sliders.

label: Attribute value
summary: The current value of a portrait attribute, as a decimal number.
details: Used in the portrait editor, a development tool of the game's engine. Vanilla sets it as the position of the attribute's slider and also writes it out next to the slider with two decimals.

label: Attribute changed
summary: Takes in a new value for a portrait attribute when its slider is moved.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it from the attribute slider of the portrait editor (a development tool of the engine) whenever the slider's value changes; the slider passes the new value itself.

label: This attribute
summary: The attribute object itself, as an object that can be handed on.
details: Attribute belongs to the game's internal GUI engine group. Going by the name and by how other types' Self functions are used (passed as an argument to other functions); vanilla never uses it on this type.

label: This availability entry
summary: The availability entry itself, as an object that can be handed on.
details: Going by its name and by how other AccessSelf functions are used. Vanilla never uses it on this type; the game documents nothing more.

label: Availability text
summary: A text describing an availability status in the friend list.
details: Vanilla shows it in the friend list window of the engine's social interface. Going by its name, it is the shown status (for example whether someone is available); the possible texts are not listed.

label: This availability entry
summary: The availability entry itself, as an object that can be handed on.
details: Going by its name and by how other types' Self functions are used (passed as an argument to other functions). Vanilla never uses it on this type; the game documents nothing more.

label: This project entry
summary: The available great project entry itself, as an object that can be handed on.
details: Going by its name and by how other AccessSelf functions are used. Vanilla never uses it on this type; the game documents nothing more.

label: Can start planning
summary: Whether planning of this great project can be started.
details: Vanilla uses it in the decisions window to show one part of an entry when planning can start and another part when it cannot.

label: Planner character
summary: The character who would plan this great project.
details: Vanilla gives this character to the great project type's functions that build an entry's tooltip and its illustration in the decisions window. Going by its name, it is the planner of the project.

label: Project description
summary: The description text of the great project entry.
details: Going by its name and its text return type only. The name appears nowhere in the game's texts or GUI files.

label: Project name
summary: The name of the great project entry, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as text in the decisions window.

label: Project status
summary: The status of the great project entry, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as text in the decisions window.

label: Project type
summary: The great project type of the entry.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data source of an element in the decisions window, so that part can show the project type's own data.

label: Unavailable reason
summary: A text explaining why the great project is not available.
details: Going by its name and its text return type only. The name appears nowhere in the game's texts or GUI files.

label: This project entry
summary: The available great project entry itself, as an object that can be handed on.
details: Going by its name and by how other types' Self functions are used (passed as an argument to other functions). Vanilla never uses it on this type; the game documents nothing more.

label: This accessory category
summary: The barbershop accessory category itself, as an object that can be handed on.
details: Going by its name and by how other AccessSelf functions are used. Vanilla never uses it on this type; the game documents nothing more.

label: Can edit color
summary: Whether the colour of this accessory category can be edited.
details: Vanilla uses it to show or hide an element of the barbershop window. Going by its name, that element is the colour editing.

label: Current color
summary: The colour currently set for this accessory category.
details: A colour with four components (CVector4f). Vanilla uses it as the tint colour of an element in the barbershop window.

label: Hovered item position
summary: The position of the item the mouse is over, as a pair of whole numbers.
details: Going by its name and its use as the selected index of an item grid in the barbershop window. The meaning of the two numbers (such as column and row) is not documented.

label: Accessory items
summary: The list of accessory items of this category.
details: Vanilla uses it as the list that fills the item grid in the barbershop window.

label: Filtered accessory items
summary: The accessory items of this category that match the current search text.
details: Vanilla uses it as the list that fills the item grid in the barbershop window. Going by its name and its pairing with GetSearchFilter, the filter is the search text.

label: Category name
summary: The name of this accessory category, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as text in the barbershop window.

label: Search text
summary: The search text currently typed for this accessory category, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as text in the barbershop window. Going by its name, it is the text used to filter the items.

label: Has color override
summary: Whether this accessory category has a colour set that replaces the natural one.
details: Vanilla uses it to show or hide the button that calls ResetColorToNatural. The exact meaning is inferred from the name.

label: Has filtered items
summary: Whether the search currently leaves any items in this category.
details: Vanilla uses it to show or hide an element of the barbershop window. The meaning is inferred from the name and its pairing with GetItemsFiltered.

label: Is color picker active
summary: Whether the colour picker of this accessory category is the active one.
details: Vanilla uses it for the pressed state of a button in the barbershop window; SelectColorPicker is used on the same kind of element.

label: Is search box visible
summary: Whether the text search of this category is shown.
details: Vanilla uses it to show or hide an element of the barbershop window. Going by the name, that element is the search box.

label: On search done
summary: Handles the player confirming the search text.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it when Return is pressed in a text box of the barbershop window.

label: On search edited
summary: Handles the search text being changed.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it when the text of the search box in the barbershop window is edited. What it does with the new text is not documented.

label: On item selected
summary: Handles the player selecting an item of this category.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it when the selection of a list in the barbershop window changes. Going by the name, the chosen accessory is applied to the character.

label: On filtered item selected
summary: Handles the player clicking an item of the filtered list.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it on click and passes the clicked entry's position in its list.

summary: Makes the colour picker of this accessory category the active one.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it on a click and on a selection change in the barbershop window. Going by the name, it opens that category's colour editing.

label: This accessory category
summary: The barbershop accessory category itself, as an object that can be handed on.

summary: Sets whether the text search of this category is shown.

label: This accessory item
summary: The barbershop accessory item itself, as an object that can be handed on.
details: Going by its name and by how other AccessSelf functions are used. Vanilla never uses it on this type; the game documents nothing more.

label: Item index
summary: The position number of the accessory item, as a whole number.

summary: The name of the accessory item, as text.

label: This accessory item
summary: The barbershop accessory item itself, as an object that can be handed on.
details: Going by its name and by how other types' Self functions are used (passed as an argument to other functions). Vanilla never uses it on this type; the game documents nothing more.

summary: The search text currently typed for this background category, as text.

details: Vanilla uses it to show or hide an element of the barbershop window. Going by the name, that element is the search box.

summary: Handles the player confirming the search text.

summary: Resets the background to the one before the preview.

label: This background category
summary: The barbershop background category itself, as an object that can be handed on.
details: Going by its name and by how other types' Self functions are used (passed as an argument to other functions). Vanilla never uses it on this type; the game documents nothing more.

summary: Sets whether the text search of this category is shown.

summary: Switches the text search of this category between shown and hidden.

details: Going by its name and by how other AccessSelf functions are used. Vanilla never uses it on this type; the game documents nothing more.

label: This camera settings

summary: The name of the barbershop category, as text.
details: Going by its name and its text return type. Vanilla never uses it on this type (the lines with GetName in the input belong to other types).

summary: The search text of the barbershop category, as text.
details: Vanilla never uses it on this type. The same function name is used on the accessory category, the background category and the pose settings in the barbershop window, which is a hint only.

label: This barbershop category
summary: The barbershop category itself, as an object that can be handed on.

label: This color picker
summary: The barbershop colour picker handler itself, as an object that can be handed on.
details: Going by its name and by how other AccessSelf functions are used. Vanilla never uses it on this type; the game documents nothing more.

label: Picked color
summary: The colour currently set in the colour picker.
details: A colour with four components (CVector4f). Vanilla uses it as the colour of an element in the barbershop window.

label: Color channels
summary: The list of colour channels the picker can edit.
details: Vanilla uses it as the list that fills an element in the barbershop window; SetColorChannel runs when the selection changes. Going by the name, a channel is one of several colours of the same item.

label: Hovered color position
summary: The position of the colour swatch the mouse is over, as a pair of whole numbers.
details: Going by its name and its use as the selected index of a grid in the barbershop window. The meaning of the two numbers (such as column and row) is not documented.

label: Has several channels
summary: Whether the item being coloured has more than one colour channel.
details: Vanilla uses it to show or hide an element of the barbershop window, presumably the channel choice. The meaning is inferred from the name.

label: Pick color
summary: Handles the player choosing a colour in the picker.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it when a colour is edited in the barbershop window. Going by the name, the chosen colour is applied.

label: This color picker
summary: The barbershop colour picker handler itself, as an object that can be handed on.
details: Going by its name and by how other types' Self functions are used (passed as an argument to other functions). Vanilla never uses it on this type; the game documents nothing more.

label: Set color channel
summary: Handles the player choosing another colour channel.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it when the selection of a list changes in the barbershop window. Going by the name, the picker then edits that channel.

label: This barbershop item
summary: The barbershop item itself, as an object that can be handed on.
details: Going by its name and by how other AccessSelf functions are used. Vanilla never uses it on this type; the game documents nothing more.

label: Item index
summary: The position number of the barbershop item, as a whole number.
details: Going by its name and its number return type only: vanilla never uses it on this type (the lines with GetIndex in the input belong to other types).

label: Item name
summary: The name of the barbershop item, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as text in the barbershop window.
